11 recommended mole removal clinics in Nagoya! Compare prices, treatment methods, and insurance coverage

"I want to have a mole removed in Nagoya, but I don't know which clinic to choose."

"I don't really understand the difference between laser and electrocautery, or whether insurance will cover it."

Many people may have the same problems as mentioned above.

There are several clinics in the Nagoya area that offer mole removal, with a variety of treatment methods and fee structures.

If you do not choose the method that is appropriate for the size and condition of your mole, you may regret the results or end up incurring extra costs.

In this article, we will explain what you need to know before getting a mole removed in Nagoya.Differences in treatment methods, market prices, and insurance coverage conditions・We will explain how to choose a medical department.

In addition, access, price range, and treatment characteristics differ.11 clinics in Nagoya areaI will introduce and compare.

Treatment methods, departments, and fees3 pointsBy organizing your information based on the following, it will be easier to choose a clinic that suits your situation.

What you can learn from this article
  • Differences and unsuitability of laser, electric scalpel, and incision methods
  • Conditions for insurance coverage and cost differences between self-pay treatment
  • How to choose and characteristics of cosmetic surgery, dermatology, and plastic surgery
Supervisor of this article

Yoshitomo Chihara

Director of Norris Beauty Clinic

Postdoctoral Researcher, Norris Cancer Center, University of Southern California;National Cancer Center PathologyHead of the club,Nara Prefectural Medical UniversityLecturer in Molecular Pathology,Saiseikai Chuwa HospitalAfter serving as head of the urology departmentnorris beauty clinicOpened a hospital.

Norris Beauty Clinic’s content production policy regarding aesthetic medicine

Norris Beauty Clinic operates with the aim of disseminating accurate and easy-to-understand information to our readers about aesthetic medicine, such as medical diets (GLP-1 receptor agonists, fat freezing, fat-dissolving injections, liposuction, etc.) and double plastic surgery.

Cosmetic treatments such as medical diets and double plastic surgery are important themes that are closely related to each individual's health condition, constitution, cost, and schedule.

We create content with an emphasis on reliability, neutrality, and safety so that our readers can calmly make choices that are suitable for them and prepare for advance counseling.

■Basic policy for content production

■Production flow

At our media, we create content through the following process.

Production flow
  1. Search needs/concerns survey
  2. Configuration design (organizing comparison standards and points to note)
  3. Writing/editing/fact checking
  4. Regular updates to the latest prices and medical system

■Regarding reliability of information

When writing articles, we use the following public institutions and highly reliable information sources.

An example of reference data for this media
  • Ministry of Health, Labor and Welfare(Medical advertising guidelines/Pharmaceuticals Act related information)
  • PMDA (Pharmaceuticals and Medical Devices Agency)
  • Japan Obesity Society・Japanese Society of Aesthetic Surgery (JSAS)Related academic societies such as
  • Consumer Affairs Agency(Related to the Specified Commercial Transactions Act and the Act on Premiums and Representations)
  • Official website information of each medical institution/pharmaceutical company

In addition, we regularly review information in response to price revisions, changes in clinic hours, updated guidelines, etc.

■Commitment to neutrality and transparency

Guaranteeing neutrality and objectivity
  • Specifies not only the benefits of each treatment but also side effects, risks, and downtime.
  • Presents points to note regarding total costs and cancellation regulations (cooling-off, etc.) for free medical treatment.
  • Do not use definitive expressions such as ``always'' or ``absolutely'' regarding changes or progress that vary from person to person.
  • Information is posted based on objective facts regardless of whether there is a partnership or not.

For detailed management structure and editorial stance, please seeNorris Beauty Clinic’s content production policy regarding aesthetic medicinePlease check.

Differences in treatment methods you should know before undergoing mole removal in Nagoya

The treatment method for mole removal isSize, depth, heightAppropriate options vary depending on the presence or absence of

Characteristics and unsuitability of the three treatment methods
  • Laser treatment: Treatment considered for small and shallow moles
  • Electrocautery: A method suitable for raised moles and neck warts
  • Incision method: A method of removing large and deep moles along with the tissue.

At clinics in the Nagoya area, we mainlyLaser treatment/electrocautery/incision methodThree types have been adopted, and each type has a clearly differentiated type of mole condition that it specializes in.

If you choose a method that is not suitable for your mole, there is a risk that it will not be removed and it will recur, or you may end up with a scar that is more noticeable than expected.

Please make sure to accurately understand the characteristics and suitability of each treatment, and then consult with your doctor before choosing the method.

Laser and electric scalpel differ in the way they scrape the skin surface, but they also differ in the equipment used and the depth of the treatment.

Lesions suspected of being malignant may require a method that allows the removed tissue to be submitted for pathological examination.

Don't just base your decision on size; also let us know if there is any change in color or bleeding at the time of your appointment.

Laser treatment is one way to remove small moles without making an incision.

Laser treatment isActs on the mole tissue through the action of the deviceIt's a method.

Since it does not involve an incision with a scalpel, the procedure can usually be performed without sutures, and theScars are relatively less noticeableIt is characterized by points.

It may be considered for small and relatively shallow moles, and doctors will examine the condition and determine whether irradiation is appropriate for areas that are more noticeable, such as the face or neck.

The treatment takes only a few minutes per area, and local anesthesia is used to minimize pain.

Laser treatment process and precautions
  • 1-2 weeks after treatment: Scab formation → Continue tape protection
  • 3-6 months: Redness and pigmentation gradually subside
  • Continuing UV protection has a big impact on the finish.
  • If the pigment is deep, multiple treatments may be required.

After the treatment, a scab will form on the affected area.1-2 weeksContinue to protect the tape until it peels off naturally.

Redness and pigmentation3-6 monthsThe skin will gradually calm down over time, so continuing to take measures against UV rays will have a big impact on the finish.

Moles where the pigment has reached deep layers may not be removed with one irradiation and may require multiple treatments.

Check the number of treatments required in advance.

Electrocautery (electrolysis) is a method suitable for raised moles and neck warts.

Electric scalpels use high-frequency current to remove mole tissue.Cauterization/evaporationThis is a treatment method that allows you to

Hemispherical moles with a raised surface, often on the neck and trunksoft fibromaIt is suitable for treating neck warts and is used for three-dimensional moles that are difficult to treat with lasers.

Since the treatment involves scraping the skin surface, it is easy to physically remove raised areas.Easy to achieve a flat finish with just one treatmentThere is an advantage.

Characteristics of moles suitable for electric scalpel
  • A hemispherical mole
  • Soft fibroma (neck wart) common on the neck and trunk
  • Three-dimensional moles that are difficult to treat with lasers
  • Cases where you want a flat finish with one treatment

Even if local anesthesia is used, you may feel pain during the injection or procedure, so be sure to check the anesthesia method in advance.

The process after the treatment is similar to laser treatment, and after a scab forms, tape protection is continued.1-2 weeksThe affected area will gradually calm down.

With electric scalpel, it may be difficult to reach deep melanin cells, and there is a risk of recurrence in moles with deep pigmentation.

Please ask your doctor to evaluate the depth before deciding on the treatment method.

The incision method is a surgical procedure in which a large, deep mole is removed and sutured.

The incision method involves cutting the skin containing the mole with a scalpel.spindle shapeThis is a surgical procedure that involves cutting and suturing.

Diameter 5mm or moreFor large moles and moles with pigment reaching deep into the dermis,Can often be removed with one treatmentThis can be said to be a major advantage.

The removed tissuepathological examinationDoctors may select it for moles that are suspected to be malignant.

What is the incision method?

The incision method is a method in which the skin is removed and sutured.

Due to sutures, after the procedure1-2 weeksStitch removal is required, and downtime is longer than with laser or electric scalpel.

The scar will remain linear, but it will become less noticeable over time by using plastic surgery suturing techniques.

Prices start from diameters over 5mm30,000 yen or moreIn many cases, the price may change as the size increases.

When choosing a clinic for treatment, one of your criteria when choosing a clinic is whether or not they have a doctor with experience in suturing techniques and post-surgery scar management.

Conditions for mole removal covered by insurance and the difference between self-pay treatment

Is mole removal covered by insurance?Purpose of removal and doctor's diagnosisDetermined by

Concept of insurance application conditions and costs
  • If there is suspicion of malignancy or functional impairment, medical treatment will be covered by insurance.
  • Removal for cosmetic purposes is at your own expense and the price varies depending on size and method.
  • A doctor determines whether insurance coverage is available through a dermoscopy test.

The distinction between cosmetic and medical purposes is not based on the patient's wishes;The doctor will make a decision after evaluating the condition of the mole.It's a thing.

By understanding in advance the cases in which insurance can be used and the cases in which it cannot be used, it will be easier to choose a clinic and estimate costs.

Costs are treated differently depending on whether there is a medical necessity for diagnosing or treating a lesion or when the purpose is simply to improve appearance.

In actual medical treatment, the amount you will be charged will vary depending on the details of the examination or surgery and how you are treated as an insurance medical institution.

If you are unsure, please first visit a dermatologist or plastic surgeon who handles insurance treatment and check whether your insurance covers it.

Check the breakdown of costs, as consultation fees and test fees may be added even with insurance treatment.

Please listen to your doctor's explanation before deciding whether it is suitable for your condition.

If there is suspicion of malignancy or functional impairment, medical treatment will be covered by insurance.

Mole removal is covered by insurance,malignant tumorThis treatment is limited to cases in which there is a suspicion that a mole is present, or if the location or size of the mole is interfering with physical function.

Specifically, there are cases where medical treatment is recognized, such as a mole on the edge of the eyelid that is obstructing vision or where the mole is suspected to be developing into skin cancer.

On the other hand, if you are concerned about your appearance or want to get rid of a complex, you will not be covered by insurance.

Main cases where insurance medical treatment is applicable
  • Suspicion of malignant tumor (skin cancer)
  • Functional impairment, such as a mole on the eyelid that obstructs vision
  • Friction and pressure are interfering with daily life.

It is not something that patients themselves can decide whether or not they will be covered by insurance; an examination and evaluation by a dermatologist or plastic surgeon is required.

In addition, even if it is removed through insurance medical treatment,Histopathological examination(examination to examine the removed mole under a microscope) may be additionally performed, and its cost will be covered by insurance.

When you visit your doctor, it will be easier for your doctor to judge your condition by taking note of changes in your mole (changes in color, shape, and size) and when you started to notice it.

Removal for cosmetic purposes is at your own expense and the price varies depending on size and method.

If you remove a mole for cosmetic purposes, health insurance generally does not cover the cost.Self-payIt is.

The price varies depending on the size of the mole and the treatment method.For moles with a diameter of 3 mm or less, removal using laser or electric scalpel isAround 5,000-15,000 yenis an example of a price guide.

When using the incision method for large moles over 5 mm in diameter or moles with deep pigmentation,30,000 yen or moreThere are many cases where this happens.

If you want to remove multiple moles at once, some clinics may charge a lower price per mole, so if you have a large number of moles, we recommend that you check in advance.

At clinics that offer bulk discounts for multiple removals, you may be able to significantly reduce the cost per treatment.

In addition, the results and scope of application differ depending on the type of equipment used for the same "laser removal," so be sure to compare not only the price but also the treatment content.

Dermoscopy helps with diagnosis and determines the need for treatment.

Dermoscopy examinationThis is a test that uses a special magnifying glass to closely observe the color, structure, and borders of a mole.

This test allows us to observe the color and structure of moles that are difficult to see with the naked eye.Doctor considers diagnosis and treatment policyThis will be the basis for this.

What is dermoscopy?

If it is determined that it is medically necessary, it will be covered by insurance.

In dermatology and plastic surgery, dermoscopy may be performed under insurance if it is deemed necessary for medical treatment.

If you decide on your own that ``it's benign, so it's okay to go to a beauty clinic'', you run the risk of overlooking a malignant tumor.

We recommend that you see a doctor if you have a mole that you are concerned about.

If it is determined that there is no suspicion of malignancy as a result of the examination, it will be difficult to remove it through insurance treatment, but it is possible to switch to a consultation at a beauty clinic at that point.

If you are concerned about a mole, please consult a dermatologist or plastic surgeon to confirm the necessary tests and treatment policy before considering where to undergo the treatment.

How to choose the department that suits you from cosmetic surgery, dermatology, and plastic surgery

The medical department where mole removal is performed isPurpose, mole condition, cost priorityThe department you should choose will change depending on the course.

How to choose a medical department by purpose
  • Cosmetic surgery: Emphasis on the beauty of the finish and the inconspicuousness of scars
  • Dermatology: If you wish to check for malignancy or receive insurance treatment
  • Plastic surgery: For cases that require large moles or incisions

Cosmetic surgery, dermatology, and plastic surgery each have different areas of expertise, and even the same mole removalScope of support and direction of finishThere is a difference.

If you choose a medical department that does not support the treatment, you may not be able to receive the treatment you want or may miss out on insurance coverage.

The name of the department alone does not determine the content of the treatment, and even within the same department, the equipment and surgical methods handled vary depending on the medical institution.

For lesions that suddenly change color or shape, it is important to consult a dermatologist before booking a cosmetic treatment.

If you wish to receive medical treatment covered by insurance, check in advance whether the clinic is covered by insurance as a medical institution.

After sorting out the condition of your mole and the purpose of treatment, choose the appropriate medical department.

Cosmetic surgery specializes in treatments that emphasize the beauty of the finish and the inconspicuousness of scars.

Cosmetic surgery is a clinic designed with the top priority being to make you look as beautiful as possible after the procedure.

In addition to laser treatment and electric scalpel removal, we also focus on suturing techniques and treatments to make scars less noticeable.Removal of moles on noticeable areas such as face and neckYou can consult with us.

Many clinics have a system in place to handle everything from counseling to treatment and aftercare, making it easy to check on the progress after surgery.

People who are suitable for cosmetic surgery
  • I want to remove moles from noticeable areas such as the face and neck
  • Top priority is given to the finish of the scar.
  • I want to remove multiple moles at once
  • Looking for consistent support from counseling to post-operative care

On the other hand, cosmetic surgery proceduresFully self-paid medical treatmentIt becomes.

Cosmetic surgery focuses on free treatment, so if you suspect malignancy or wish to receive insurance coverage, you will need to visit a dermatologist or plastic surgeon.

Prices vary depending on the clinic, but3mm or lessIf it's a moleAround 5,000-15,000 yenPlease consider this as a guide.

If you want to remove multiple moles at once, or if you prioritize the beauty of the finished product, please visit a cosmetic surgeon.

Dermatology is suitable for cases where malignancy is suspected or those who wish to receive insurance treatment.

Dermatology is a medical department that medically evaluates the malignancy risk of moles and then decides on a treatment plan.

Dermoscopy examinationWe carefully observe the color, shape, and border of the mole and differentiate it from malignant melanoma.

If a doctor determines that the mole is suspected to be malignant, or if the mole is found to be interfering with daily life due to friction or pressure, it will be covered by insurance medical treatment.

If the removal is covered by insurance, the cost can be reduced to a few thousand yen with a 30% burden.

However, as removal for cosmetic purposes is not covered by insurance, this department is suitable for those who want to prioritize medical decisions over aesthetic results.

When visiting a dermatologist, the examination will go more smoothly if you summarize in advance any changes you are concerned about, such as the size of the mole, changes in color, and presence or absence of bleeding.

Do not judge by yourself whether it is malignant or not, first consult a dermatologist.Decide on the removal method after undergoing dermoscopy.please.

Plastic surgeons handle incisions and sutures for large moles and cases that require incisions.

Plastic surgery is a medical department that specializes in the reconstruction and repair of skin and tissues, and has strengths in removing large moles and moles that extend deep into the skin.

diameterMole larger than 5mmFor moles with large protuberances that cannot be treated with lasers, we use the incision and suture method to remove them.

With the incision method, the technique used to suture the skin greatly affects the outcome, but plastic surgeons have specialized training in suturing techniques, soTreatment considering scarscan be expected.

People who are suitable for plastic surgery
  • I have a large mole over 5mm in diameter.
  • I have a mole with a large bump that cannot be treated with a laser.
  • I want to achieve both medical precision and post-surgical results.
  • I am considering insurance coverage for a large mole that is suspected to be malignant.

Insurance coverage is determined in the same way as a dermatologist, so if you have a large mole that is suspected to be malignant, a visit to a plastic surgeon is a reasonable option.

After removal by incision, it will take 1 to 2 weeks for the stitches to be removed, and redness and pigmentation may continue for 3 to 6 months.

Be sure to check with your doctor about the expected downtime before your procedure.

Among the three departments of cosmetic surgery, dermatology, and plastic surgery, plastic surgery is an option if you want both medical precision and post-surgery results.

Market price for mole removal in Nagoya and estimated cost by size and number of moles

The cost of mole removal isTreatment method and mole sizevaries greatly depending on

Rates by size and method and how to use discounts
  • Lasers and electric scalpels cost around 5,000 to 15,000 yen for diameters of 3 mm or less.
  • There are many clinics where the cost per item is cheaper by removing multiple items at once.
  • The incision method generally costs more than 30,000 yen for a diameter of more than 5 mm.

At clinics in the Nagoya area, if you have a small mole with a diameter of 3 mm or less,Around 5,000 to 15,000 yen per pieceis the standard price range.
